experiment: Lab experiment 2c: fiscal sensitivity with a drifting baseline
label: Lab experiment
status: associations in a model-estimated term premium; not causal; a drifting baseline can understate a genuine fiscal effect
reporting_units: basis points of premium per 1 point of GDP of fiscal deterioration (bp = -100 x coefficient on the balance, surplus positive); positive = larger deficits go with a higher premium. Baselines in percentage points of premium.

text: 4. **Declared answer rule** (applied to C1; reported for C2 to C4, with agreement or disagreement stated):
- "**both retreats survive**": the early and the late retreat are each at least half their C0 size **and** each 95% interval excludes zero;
- "**only the 2008 break survives**": the late retreat meets that test and the early one does not;
- "**only the early fade survives**": the early retreat meets it and the late one does not;

coming_back_rule_text: The link counts as reappearing only if the latest filtered estimate's 95% interval lies entirely above the post-2008 range of the filtered path, that is, its lower bound is above the highest filtered point estimate from fiscal year 2009 to the year before the latest. Otherwise it does not count as reappearing, however much the line has risen.

c1_vs_c0.note: same states (a, c, b); q_a = 0 under C0, on the boundary

retreat_intervals.method: statsmodels simulation smoother at the maximum-likelihood variances (conditional on them); each draw gives a full fiscal-slope path; the retreat is computed on each draw
retreat_intervals.point: the retreat computed on the smoothed path (not the draws' mean)

paths_from_note: each path is reported from the first fiscal year in which the fiscal slope's own diffuse variance is zero; for C0 to C3 this is the end of the model's diffuse period (Experiment 2's convention), and for C4, whose FY2008 shift coefficient stays diffuse until FY2008 although it does not load before then, it is the same year as C0. Implementation note written in T8 after the first run stopped on C4 (its paths were empty before FY2009), while checking that C4's smoothed values are finite; it follows from the model, changes only where C4's reported paths start, and does not enter any FY1982 value, retreat or rule result

C0.role: anchor: Experiment 2's main version (ACM + debt). Must reproduce outputs/lab/fiscal-sensitivity/results.json acm_debt within the cross-platform tolerance below, with rule results exactly equal

step_check.definition: fixed slopes for FY up to step_fy - 1 and from step_fy, shared constant and debt control, fitted values without noise, smoothed with C1's estimated variances

C2.role: as C1 without the debt control (debt behaves like a trend; the drifting baseline may take that role)

t8b.label: added after the results existed (T8b, after review)

C3.drift_is_on: the trend's growth rate (pp per year per year), not the baseline's level
C3.collapses_toward: a straight-line trend (constant growth), not C0, if its drift variance were zero

t8b.variance_uncertainty_definition: log-variance parameters drawn from a normal with the fit's inverse-Hessian covariance (400 parameter draws x 10 simulation-smoother paths = 4000 draws, seed 20261023); point as reported; the declared test applied with the reported shares of C0

c1_profile.definition: log q_a fixed at C1's estimate plus offsets -6.00 to +3.00 in steps of 0.25, other variances by maximum likelihood (same starting points); region: likelihood-ratio statistic against C1's fit at most 3.84 (chi-square(1), 95%); retreat intervals from the declared draws and seed at each value

c1_step_check_fixed_anchor.note: from FY1982 (the rule's anchor year) and FY2000; C1's path is flat before FY2000, so its peak year carries little meaning
